findings.finding: The 2012 INS census/projection reference uses 266 commune-labeled units, including municipal arrondissements within special city communes. Atlas represents five Maradi/Tahoua arrondissement units separately while Niamey is a composite with six ADM3 source members. Neighboring special-city granularity is inconsistent unless a distinct product-purpose rationale is documented.
findings.handoff: Create a bounded engineering/semantic follow-up to compare official statutory commune/arrondissement roles and decide consistent city aggregation; do not edit hierarchy in this packet.
findings.confidence: high on source vocabulary/count and Atlas representation; legal present-day equivalence and geometry comparison remain unresolved.

findings.finding: DGAT’s current summary attributes 63 Moughataas to RGPH 2024. An official SNGM / Plan d’Action 2021–2023 document dated 2022-01-25 reports 61 Moughataas, 15 Wilayas, and 218 communes (page 6), establishing an earlier dated count but not reconciling the later count. An AMI government announcement says six arrondissements became Moughataas on 2021-09-08 and names their parent Wilayas: Adel Bagrou/Hodh Ech Chargui; Touil/Hodh El Gharbi; Lexeiba/Gorgol; Male/Brakna; Tékane/Trarza; Wompou/Guidimaka. All six names are absent from the pinned 57-feature 2020 MRT ADM2 source and are not present in the Atlas Mauritania source classes represented here. This is a specific likely post-vintage coverage gap; the 61-to-63 relationship, exact legal decrees, full current roster, and reusable polygons remain unresolved.
findings.handoff: Obtain exact decrees and licensed/current official polygons for the six named units; reconcile the 2022 strategy count of 61, the RGPH 2024 DGAT count of 63, the 57 pinned 2020 features, and the Atlas 69-member area scope. Do not infer missing units or draw/import boundaries from counts, SVG, or names alone.
findings.confidence: High that the cited official documents report the stated counts at their respective dates and that AMI reports six names/date/parent Wilayas; low for the legal roster transition, exact geometries, and full-current reconciliation.

findings.finding: Ten scoped locations are pieces of five RESOLVE 2017 ecoregions, attached to four underlying Moughataas and grouped as locality-plus-ecoregion fragments. RESOLVE describes ecological regions, not political subdivisions; its layer has a separate data-last-edit timestamp. A legal/semantic purpose for treating fragments as geography locations and exact union/boundary equivalence has not been established.
findings.handoff: Review source-member polygons, exact clipped geometry, piece completeness and intended non-administrative tier semantics; retain as unresolved until tested.

findings.finding: geoBoundaries metadata labels the 2012 NER ADM3 extraction CC BY 3.0 but cites CityPopulation; CityPopulation terms distinguish its population data from third-party geospatial/maps. Rights to redistribute the geometry bundle are therefore ambiguous from inspected evidence.
findings.handoff: Do not redistribute downloaded NER source geometry. Preserve pinned URL, exact SHA-256, metadata, terms capture hash and restoration instructions; request authoritative license-chain evidence before a geometry-bearing correction.

findings.finding: Measured source-vintage overlap diagnostic for all 204 scoped NER 2012 ADM3 shapes against all 67 pinned NER 2018 ADM2 shapes. 172/204 have at least 90% in their maximum candidate; 32 are below 90%; 54 reach 99%. Low examples include Agadez (77.6% Tchirozérine), Maradi I (38.4% Madarounfa), Maradi III (59.3% Maradi). These values cannot determine a legal parent and may result from vintage changes or special-city semantics.
findings.handoff: Review all 32 low-overlap rows with official dated parent/city sources; compare source versions and identify source-vintage drift versus true mis-parenting. Do not edit the graph based on overlap alone.
findings.confidence: high that the source polygon intersections reproduce under the recorded method; low for legal interpretation.

findings.finding: The official 2012 INS reference yields 190 exact normalized name/department matches, 10 resolved spelling/special-city aliases, and four candidate rows under the `Tibiri (Doutchi)` department whose relationship to the Atlas `Tibiri` parent role remains unresolved. Special-city rows are represented with different granularity in this scoped branch: Maradi I–III and Tahoua I–II remain separate while the six Niamey ADM3 member units feed one composite city.
findings.handoff: Obtain a current official statutory register and source-to-Atlas role crosswalk for the four Tibiri(Doutchi) rows and all four special cities; decide and document neighboring granularity before hierarchy correction.
findings.confidence: high for extraction and 2012 statistical row matches; historical administrative law, current status and boundary correctness remain open.
